text: thats really good news. now, how about what if we were to compile the world from a cached state, as, clearly, when making the game, its not like i am going to be recompiling an entirely new map, its going to be incrementally adding more and more
resolution: Explained how cached/incremental compile changes the scaling model: the previous TS/Zig parity benchmark was a cold full-world bake, while a cached compile should track dirty chunks/assets and rebuild only changed RLE chunks, geometry chunks, manifests, and content-addressed assets. Also called out the remaining monolithic-file bottleneck: if the final gamefile is always rewritten as one blob, output assembly stays O(total bytes), so the durable direction is chunk/content-addressed map payloads plus a small manifest update.
